title: Covering family of finite-reduction models
statement: Let X be Noetherian and A a commutative Noetherian J-adically complete ring. Let M be a locally derived complete object over the completed coefficient ring B on the coefficient pro-etale model site, whose residue is the comparison of a bounded etale A/J-complex C with locally constant finite-type cohomology and Tor amplitude [a,b], a <= b, as in [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons]. Then there is a small covering family V_i -> final of affine weakly contractible objects and, for each i, a bounded finite-projective A-cochain complex P_i, such that for every n the actual derived reductions modulo J^(n+1) of (B tensor P_i)|V_i and M|V_i are isomorphic. No completeness on these slices, coherent markings, or comparison functor on arbitrary sieve members is asserted.

source.place: first half through the choice of an affine weakly contractible cover (Tag 09C6)

proof.text: Apply the normalized stalk-tower family theorem. It gives the covering, its affine and actual slice weak-contractibility properties, and a normalized algebraic quotient tower on each member with individual finite-level isomorphisms to the actual reductions of M.

On each covering member, exact countable products of A-modules give a product of the restricted algebraic tower in D(A). Construct a Roos derived-limit triangle. Apply perfect inverse-limit reconstruction over the J-adically complete ring A to the normalized transitions and the perfect residue level. It makes the limit perfect and its projection-induced algebraic reductions isomorphisms. Choose its bounded finite-projective representative P, reverse its marking when applying scalar extension, and compose with each projection-induced reduction isomorphism.

For every level use the completed constant perfect reduction comparison with the tower extension and its adjunction. Apply exact finite constant realization to the algebraic reduction isomorphism from step 2, and compose with the tower marking from step 1. These three actual isomorphisms identify the local reductions of the constant completed P and M. Keep the same covering, support interval and finite projective terms; no compatibility of local markings or completeness on slices is asserted.
